key_insight: Frozen-host quantum embedding captures molecular environmental effects from finite hosts to periodic crystals while keeping active-subsystem calculations near gas-phase cost.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables lower-cost modeling of adsorption, solvation, and substrate-modified optical responses without recalculating the full environment.
method: Compute the host once and represent it using Gaussian-fitted electron density and nuclear charges.
Separate periodic electrostatics into explicit near-field and fast-multipole far-field contributions.
Embed molecular DFT, real-time TDDFT, or correlated excited-state calculations; use analytic gradients for active-subsystem relaxation.
evidence_signal: Reported tests reproduce periodic CO–MgO interaction energy within 0.44 kJ/mol at 27× lower cost and a supermolecular CC2 solvent shift within 0.01 eV at over 500× lower cost.
watch_item: Because the host is frozen, accuracy should be checked when guest-induced host polarization or structural relaxation is substantial.
paper_title: Quantum Embedding from Molecular to Crystalline Environments at the Cost of a Gas-Phase Calculation
